  MINUTES
  VERNON BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY COMMISSION
  SPECIAL MEETING

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER

  FLAG SALUTE

  Chair Condon led the Flag Salute.

  Commissioner Ybarra moved and Commissioner Sachdeva seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called and the motion carried 6-0,
  Commission Member Browne absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following item:

  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the September 12, 2024, Special Business and Industry
  Commission Meeting Minutes.

  NEW BUSINESS

  2.  Proposed Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-2026 General Fee Schedule

  Interim Finance Director Decavalles-Hughes presented the staff report and Tony
  Thrasher, Willdan Project Manager, presented a PowerPoint on the Fee Schedule.

  Commissioner Browne arrived at 9:10 a.m.

  Commissioner Browne stated some building fees are lower than other cities and some
  are higher in comparison. She asked if there are plans to reduce those fees, for
  example, the Conditional Use Permit and Certificate of Occupancy could be more in
  line with the average. She inquired why administrative fees may not be at cost recovery.

  Consultant Thrasher noted that fees (particularly for Conditional Use Permits or
  Building Permits) are a multi-departmental activity so there is no clear comparison with
  other cities. It may not be known what elements are included in other cities’ fees.
  Certain administrative fees are subsidized, such as certified copies, that do not affect
  a city’s bottom line.

  Chair Condon addressed how fees impact small businesses, such as businesses with
  multiple locations. He raised a question on certain fees collected from businesses.
  Finance Director Decavalles-Hughes noted that some fees are considered taxes and
  are passed by voters and would require a vote to be changed.

  Commissioner Ybarra requested that staff add a discussion item on the next agenda
  relating to business license fees, presenting options to the Commission. Consultant
  Thrasher stated that because the Business License Fee is a tax, it must be taken to the
  voters.

  Chair Condon stated that the first fee businesses see is the Certificate of Occupancy
  and requested a review of this fee.

  Consultant Thrasher responded to cost vs comparison questions by Commissioner
  Sablock and explained the nuances of costs to provide a service compared to other
  agencies, and noted the proposed suggested fees are at full cost. Any fee above the
 Docusign Envelope ID: C8468CA1-4547-40B9-ABD0-B4FC7280658E

  full cost becomes a tax rather than a fee and would have to be approved by a vote of
  the public.

  Commissioner Ybarra asked how some fees can be increased and how subsidies can
  be made for smaller businesses, possibly finding a way to incorporate a multi-step or
  tiered fee schedule to keep the Certificate of Occupancy costs for small businesses or
  businesses that have multiple locations more reasonable. It was requested that the
  business license fees for multiple locations be placed on the next Business and Industry
  Commission Agenda.

  City Administrator Saeki stated that taking the fees above cost recovery would require
  a vote of the people but reducing them is an action of the Council.

  There was discussion regarding the fees for business owners having multiple business
  locations and how to reduce the costs to make the fees reasonable. City Administrator
  Saeki indicated that the topic could be discussed at the next Business and Industry
  Commission meeting.

  Commissioner Browne asked about the comparison of calculations by other agencies
  related to the Certificate of Occupancy that is applied to each business location.

  Consultant Thrasher explained that other agencies’ processes for calculating
  Certificate of Occupancy costs are based on residential population and the process
  factors in industrial encounters that impact the cost calculation. Vernon’s fees are
  based off what is typically seen in the community demographic, which is why the cost
  calculation is higher than other agencies. Consultant Thrasher noted that subsidizing
  the fees by categories complicates the schedule.

  City Administrator Saeki noted that other cities may not be providing power and utilities
  to businesses and permits processed in-house in Vernon that are not reflected in their
  Certificate of Occupancy costs, which sets the City apart.

  Chair Condon suggested comparing business license fees with other cities and stated
  that the City’s Temporary Occupancy Fee could be eliminated and folded in with the
  Final Occupancy Fee, suggesting that the City not have a separate charge for the
  temporary permit. He asked for these items to be added to the next agenda.

  Consultant Thrasher noted there are subsidies in some fees such as copies and most
  do not make a difference in the bottom line.

  Chair Condon invited public comment.

  There being no public comment, Chair Condon invited a motion to Receive and File.
  Commissioner Ybarra moved to approve the staff recommendation. The motion was
  recalled.

  MOTION
  Commissioner Browne moved and Commissioner Sachdeva seconded a motion to
  recommend staff provide options to the City Council to subsidize or tier the Certificate
  of Occupancy Fee for small businesses.

  Commissioner Browne amended her motion to add staff look back at prior historical fee
  structures that were tiered or bracketed as related to businesses with multiple locations.

  MOTION AS AMENDED
  The motion as amended carried unanimously.

  MOTION
  Commissioner Ybarra moved and Vice Chair Morfin seconded a motion to receive and
  file the User Fee Study and proposed FY 2025-26 General Fee Schedule and request
  that staff present the proposed General Fee Schedule to Council for review and
  adoption at a public hearing on April 1, 2025. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  ORAL REPORTS

  3.  Brief Reports, Announcements, or Directives to Staff

  City Administrator Saeki provided the following announcements:

  •  MetroLink Community Meeting – City Administrator Saeki stated staff continues
  to prioritize discussions with Metro regarding its proposed Link US Project
  Malabar Yard modifications in Vernon. He indicated Metro is planning an open
  house/community meeting and have set a tentative date of March 26, 2025. He
  indicated relevant updates regarding the project will be provided to the
  Commission when available.
  •  Business Breakfast – City Administrator Saeki asked that everyone keep a
  lookout for details on the next Business Breakfast in April. He indicated
  breakfasts are designed to be an open forum for the business community, and
  to speak about topics that are most important and provide an opportunity to
  network and connect with other Vernon businesses.
